correctness.rationale: For odd abelian A, every element at in the nontrivial coset is an involution, so its cyclic subgroup is a distinct order-two leaf adjacent only to the trivial subgroup; every other cyclic subgroup lies in A. Hence the cyclic-subgroup Hasse graph is exactly C(A)^* with |A| leaves attached and ε(Dih(A))=ε(A)+|A|. Tărnăuceanu's nilpotent theorem gives ε(A)≥ε(C_m), equality only for cyclic A. For odd m, the coprime product formula gives ε(C_{2m})=2ε(C_m)+τ(m). Writing f(m)=τ(m)+ε(C_m), one has f(p^a)=2a+1≤p^a for odd prime powers, equality only at 3, and for coprime u,v>1, f(uv)=f(u)f(v)-ε(C_u)ε(C_v)<f(u)f(v). Thus f(m)≤m with equality exactly m=3, proving the comparison and equality case. I also independently checked f(m)≤m through odd m<1000, with equality only at 3; this finite check is corroborative, not the universal proof.
risks: Oddness of A is essential to make every outside element an involution and every added subgroup a leaf.
The result proves the even-order conjecture only for the generalized-dihedral family.

originality.rationale: The primary 2023 theorem covers nilpotent groups and all odd-order groups and explicitly leaves arbitrary even order as a conjecture. The current cyclic-subgroup-graph paper gives the ordinary dihedral formula ε(D_{2m})=ε(C_m)+m, but its inspected family list and table do not cover generalized dihedral groups with noncyclic odd abelian kernel. Resultary searches found the audited theorem, a later generalized-dicyclic companion, and unrelated generalized-dihedral graph invariants, but no earlier statement implying the generalized-dihedral edge formula plus sharp cyclic comparison. The theorem is therefore original to the best of the inspected evidence.
